column2: Johannes Brand has died in office after nearly a quarter century at the head of the Orange Free State. Under him the republic fought, negotiated, built courts and schools, compensated for the loss of the diamond fields and learned to survive through careful diplomacy. His death closes an era. column2: The railway has made an old Free State grievance impossible to ignore: customs are collected at distant ports on goods ultimately consumed by inland burghers. President Reitz can now accept a customs union with the Cape Colony, sharing revenue and tying Bloemfontein more closely to the southern ports, or preserve an independent tariff policy and lean toward the sister republic beyond the Vaal. This is not a choice between trade and isolation, but between two competing economic geographies for the Free State.

column2: Gold from the Witwatersrand has given the South African Republic something its impoverished frontier government once lacked: the metal, credit and confidence to put republican sovereignty into everyday circulation. Legislation for a state mint has been followed by machinery for Pretoria, and the Volksraad must decide whether the republic will strike its own pond and shillings under the Vierkleur or continue relying primarily on sterling and imported coin. A national coinage would be expensive, but every Kruger pond would make the independence of the republic tangible in a merchant's hand.
